key_idea: Because the zones (SCCs) form a chain in the condensation, the final graph may contain every edge inside an SCC and every edge from an earlier SCC to a later one; subtract the existing edges.
sketch: Run Tarjan's SCC directly on the adjacency matrix in O(n^2) for n = 2500 and collect component sizes s_i. The statement guarantees all zones can be visited in one walk, so the condensation is totally ordered and the maximum edge count is sum s_i(s_i-1) + sum_{i<j} s_i s_j = (n^2 - sum s_i^2)/2 + sum s_i^2 - n. The answer is that minus the number of ones in the input. Pitfalls: reading 6.25M integers needs fast input (getchar), recursion depth is up to 2500 which is fine, and the count needs 64-bit only marginally (about 6M).
